interface: Helpers over unchanged canonical evaluationMatrix, testMatrix, auxiliaryCode and ambiguity
exact_goals: For A:I×J and B:J×K, rank A+rank B≤rank(A*B)+card J.
For C⊆F^I and S⊆I, dim(range restriction_S C)+dim(ambiguity C Sᶜ)=dim C, and the corresponding generator-matrix restriction rank formula.

supportPoints g y is the image under the exact rowOrder equivalence of the actual nonzero coordinates of y. For r=dim(auxiliaryCode g), b=dim(ambiguity(auxiliaryCode g)(supportPoints g y)ᶜ), prove 2r−2b−weight y≤rank(testMatrix g y).
The real-valued rank of the canonical testMatrix on boolWord x has unit bounded differences under one Boolean coordinate update.
proof_route: Sylvester: restrict A.mulVecLin to range(B), apply rank-nullity, and inject its kernel into ker(A). Restriction: identify the coordinate restriction kernel with ambiguity(complement) via the code subtype and use rank-nullity; rows of a restricted matrix span the image code. Factor testMatrix exactly as the evaluation matrix on its nonzero point support times its transpose, reindexing through rowOrder. Sylvester and restriction give the rank lower bound. For Lipschitz, a one-coordinate word difference has weight≤1, its testMatrix rank≤1 by CombinedOrthogonality, and matrix-rank subadditivity gives both rank inequalities.
failed_approaches: First elaboration found differing synthesized DecidableEq instances in specialized Finset complements; generic restriction lemmas now expose DecidableEq I explicitly, so their complements specialize consistently.
Finite sum reindexing initially used sum_coe_sort backwards and a mismatched sum_filter rewrite; replaced by forward subtype-sum conversion and sum_subset with zero terms outside actual support.

Canonical weight uses a classical decision procedure in its filter while supportPoints initially uses the available finite decision procedure. An extensional equality of filters resolves the difference; no definition was altered.
